correctness.rationale: A generic centered plane intersects both opposite faces x_i=±a_i in edges iff each weighted absolute normal X=a|u1|,Y=b|u2|,Z=c|u3| satisfies the strict triangle inequality against the other two. Thus six-sided sections occur exactly in the spherical cone spanned by (b,a,0),(c,0,a),(0,c,b) in the positive octant; otherwise centered symmetry and polygon geometry give four edges, with equality sets measure zero. An independent SymPy determinant gives -2abc and exact scalar products bc,ab,ac, yielding p6=4/pi arctan[2abc/(alpha beta gamma+bc gamma+ac beta+ab alpha)] by the classical solid-angle identity. AM-GM proves Q/(abc)>=5sqrt2 with equality only a=b=c; continuity along (t,1,1), t>=1, and limit0 proves every probability in (0,4/pi atan(sqrt2/5)]. The known cube equality 1-6/pi asin(1/3) is algebraically consistent. The actual verify_probability.py was read; its Monte Carlo trials cannot prove the general all-positive-a,b,c theorem, which the cone/AM-GM proof establishes.

originality.rationale: Lonke's full 1998 work explicitly treats Haar central sections of a cube and its expected vertex count; in dimension three that computes the already-known equal-edge probability and is credited, not new. The exact unequal a,b,c law cannot be obtained by affinely stretching a Haar plane because the plane distribution changes; Lonke's equal-cube statement is not a broader-aspect-ratio result. Abas's orthotope width distribution is a different invariant, and the van Oosterom–Strackee spherical triangle identity is a standard calculation method. No covering unequal-box shape law or sharp all-aspect-ratio rigidity theorem found in actual inspected statements; inaccessible/hidden historical stereology remains a residual risk.
